## Report: Aaronson, “Why Philosophers Should Care About Computational Complexity”

I took the title/opening’s central question: **Does computational complexity theory have philosophical relevance, and what does it add beyond computability?** Range: analytic philosophy topics listed in the abstract. Asked: a case for relevance. The supplied text stops in Section 7; later topics (quantum, economics, CTCs) are not judged here.

### Parts and marks

| Part | Mark | What holds it / what would break it |
|---|---|---|
| P1. Polynomial/exponential gap is philosophically distinct. | **Held** | Job: show complexity differs from computability. Shrink the gap to n vs 2n: paper says too sensitive. Widen to finite/infinite: loses finding vs verifying. |
| P2. P vs NP revives the Entscheidungsproblem story. | **Held** | Job: explain why Hilbert’s dream is not over. Poke: if P=NP, proof search becomes practical; if P≠NP, it stays dead. |
| P3. Complexity can formalize evolvability. | **Held if** | Held only if the job “complexity can settle evolutionary speed” is real. Paper admits it cannot prove Gödel’s intuition. What would settle it: lower bounds on evolutionary algorithms. |
| P4. “Known integer” means efficiently generatable/provable. | **Held** | Contrast: 2^43112609−1 vs “first prime larger.” Swap “known” = “definable”: the second becomes known, contradicting the intuition. |
| P5. Lookup table shows computability cannot rule out AI. | **Held** | By finite conversation bound + computability: fB is computable. Poke: finite vs infinite conversation length changes the conclusion. |
| P6. Speculation *: Turing Test passers need exponential resources. | **Unknown** | No test run. Would be settled by a resource lower bound or an efficient program. |
| P7. Cobham/infinity gives a limiting case for logical omniscience. | **Held** for the limiting case; **Held if** for full solution. | Cobham theorem holds the limiting case. Full solution held only if the doubtful job “complexity solves omniscience” is real; paper admits objections. |
| P8. Complexity formalizes non-vacuous reductions (waterfall). | **Held** | By P-completeness: reducing class must be weaker to avoid vacuity. Poke: use P as reducing class; all P problems become complete. |
| P9. PAC learning addresses induction/grue. | **Held if** | Held by PAC theory, but paper lists drawbacks and does not claim full Hume solution. |
| P10. Complexity will ultimately be more relevant than computability. | **Loose** | Could be replaced by the opposite, or by “both matter.” No test given. |
| P11. Why complexity hasn’t influenced philosophy: suspected communication failure. | **Loose** | Could swap for social reasons, math barrier, timing. Paper offers several, no evidence. |
| P12. Modesty/scope: not dissolving problems, analytic only. | **Fixed** | Owner set these limits; not tested. |
| P13. Asymptotic explanatory force needs philosophical analysis. | **Unknown** | Would be settled by an account of why polynomial/exponential asymptotics explain practice. |

### Whole-explanation checks

**Flip.** The main thesis—complexity matters—would break if every listed topic got no new insight from complexity. The paper shows specific cases where computability is silent (Turing Test, logical omniscience, induction), so the flip fails there. P10 and P11 flip easily: if complexity had influenced philosophy, the “communication failure” story would be wrong. They are loose.

**Direction.** Mostly forward: from complexity results to philosophical implications. P4 works backward from “known” to a criterion, but that is conceptual analysis, not a causal claim. Fine.

**Answer hidden in starting points?** No. The essay does not start by assuming “complexity matters.” It argues from P vs NP, PAC, Cobham, etc. But P10 is a projection from current successes.

**Jobs: where from?** Most jobs are **given** by the paper: show relevance, answer objections, explain non-influence, stay modest. I added one: each listed topic must have a concrete complexity result, not just hand-waving. That added job is met for supplied topics; not met for abstract-only topics.

**Pull.** P10 (complexity more relevant) pulls against P12 (modesty). P3 (evolvability) pulls against P13 (asymptotic explanatory force): the paper admits complexity is far from proving the needed lower bounds. P11 (communication failure) pulls against P1 (gap is natural): if the gap is so natural, why no influence? The paper gives social/communication answers.

**Catch-alls.** “Several other topics” in the abstract is a stated scope, not a hidden bin. No gauge needed because the paper lists the topics.

**Change list.** Covers: P vs NP resolution; efficient vs lookup-table AI; finite vs infinite conversation; weaker vs stronger reducing class; different hypothesis classes in PAC; polynomial vs exponential evolutionary time. Leaves out: non-analytic philosophy, other intersections (programming languages, distributed systems, Kolmogorov complexity), proofs of speculation *, resolutions of the philosophical problems. Most are said up front.

**Rivals.** Strongest rival: computability already did the important work; complexity is engineering. The paper rules this out for several topics by showing computability is silent. For other topics, not fully.

**Patches.** The paper narrows claims openly: “not dissolving,” “no proof,” “not yet close.” No hidden narrowing found.

### Where each part came from

P1–P9 are mostly **built** into philosophical arguments, but they **borrow** results from complexity theory (P vs NP, Cobham, PAC, descriptive complexity). P6 is **unknown**/asserted as a speculation. P10–P11 are **asserted**. P12 is **fixed**. P13 is **unknown**.

### What would make it harder to vary

1. Prove or disprove P6: a resource lower bound for passing the Turing Test.
2. Give one concrete complexity theorem that settles a philosophical puzzle, not just reframes it.
3. Run the rival: find a philosophical problem where computability and complexity give different answers, and show the complexity answer is better.

### What this does not show

Hard to vary is not truth. The essay’s overall thesis is not proven. Many parts are perspectives, not solutions. The paper says so.

### One next step

Pick P6 or P7. Try to remove the complexity part. If the philosophical problem stays exactly as it was, that part is idle for that topic. If it changes, name the change that does the work.
